provenance: Local production candidate builds. Final measurements include the editor snapshot fix. Recorded IDs/revisions below; deployment verified separately. Not authenticated production-user timings.

conditions.application: real production Next build; synthetic isolated Mongo replica set; one tenant/300 invoices; no production credentials
conditions.cold: new Next process (health-only readiness probe) plus new browser context/cache, each route independently; process startup excluded
conditions.warm: same browser/store/process: client link to other route then return, with assets cached
conditions.skeleton: First requestAnimationFrame callback where a main aria-busy skeleton or route status skeleton has a visible DOM layout. This is not a guaranteed paint timestamp: rAF precedes paint and a later long task may delay paint. Use FCP separately.
conditions.ready: First rAF callback where the data-derived dashboard action section, or all 30 visible-layout invoice detail links without loading status, exist in DOM. Not a guaranteed paint timestamp or completion of optional charts. Server-rendered data may become ready before hydration; controls readiness is measured separately.
conditions.ttfb: Navigation/Resource Timing requestStart to responseStart; separate unthrottled direct API serial samples
conditions.limits: Small controlled laboratory sample, no production geography/concurrency/real-user percentile claim; app warm-up, CPU contention and browser emulation affect results. PDF and KSeF endpoints/provider actions excluded.
conditions.controlsReady: First rAF-visible dashboard refresh button with its natural React onClick prop, or invoice search input with its natural React onChange prop. A hydration signal, not an executed action or a guaranteed paint timestamp. Data-and-controls readiness is the maximum of readyMs and controlsReadyMs.
conditions.observerWork: Read-only rAF probes scan only pending metrics: data rows stop being inspected after first data-ready, control layout is inspected only once its natural React handler exists, all layout probes stop after data and controls are ready, and a warm route reset starts them again. The first-ready criteria are unchanged. Earlier version-1 runs kept scanning settled rows during hydration; timings across these versions are not directly paired.
conditions.warmHydrationGuard: Each collection waits for both data and control hydration before continuing. Before warm navigation, the visible Next link must also have its natural React onClick prop. Every warm navigation must preserve a unique document identity; full reloads fail the benchmark. Earlier reports without this guard measured warm navigation after client-rendered data readiness.
conditions.fcp: Navigation Paint Timing first-contentful-paint, measured separately from DOM skeleton and data readiness; navigation values only apply to cold document entries.
conditions.host: Browser, application server and MongoDB are co-located. Run without concurrent builds/browser benchmarks. Host limits are recorded separately when available. A laboratory relative comparison, not a real-user loading SLO.
conditions.providerGuard: Next uses loopback-only.cjs; Chromium uses a non-listening external proxy plus resolver isolation, and CDP Network.setBlockedURLs blocks KSeF/PDF/export-pack requests before navigation. No Playwright routing is installed, so normal HTTP caching remains enabled. Baseline had zero requests matching these additional CDP guards.
conditions.navigationTiming: Navigation Timing belongs only to cold-entry document navigation. Warm-client records retain the original document navigation entry; use their route ready/skeleton measurements and API Resource Timing separately.
